---
title: T3 - Environment
jupyter: python3
---


The environment plays a key role in the spread of typhoid. It is part of the disease: `ty.Typhoid` tracks the colony-forming units (CFUs) in the environment as `cfu`, and infects people through it (the `environment` route) as well as by contact. Its parameters are the disease's, e.g. `shedding_rate`, `decay_rate`, `env_rel_trans`, and `teer` (the environmental exposure rate). Here we switch off contact transmission (`exposure2contact_rate=0`) to see the environmental route on its own.


```{python}
import starsim as ss
import typhoidsim as ty

# Define high-level simulation parameters
pars = dict(
    start    = 2000,          # Starting year
    dur      = ss.years(1),   # Duration of the simulation
    dt       = ss.days(1),    # Timestep of 1 day
    verbose  = 0,             # Do not print details of the run
)

# The population
ppl = ss.People(10_000)

# The disease, which includes the environment the population is affected by, and which can carry the pathogen
typhoid = ty.Typhoid(exposure2contact_rate=0) # Transmission only through the environment

sim = ss.Sim(
    pars=pars,
    people=ppl, 
    diseases=typhoid,
    )
sim.run()
sim.plot('typhoid_cfu')
```

```{python}
#| collapsed: false
sim.results
```

### Environmental dynamics 

This model of the environment changes over time:
- grows (↑↑) by receiving CFUs from infectious individuals (at `shedding_rate` times their infectiousness);
- decays (↓↓) according to a decay rate that you can specify (`decay_rate`).
